metadata.note: The Gulf and Ship Island Railroad (perpetual charter 1882; receivership 1892-1896) built Gulfport - Hattiesburg (passenger service from 1897), Hattiesburg - Jackson (1900), the Laurel Branch Saratoga - Laurel (1900/01) and the 'semicircular' Columbia Branch Maxie - Columbia (1900/01) - Mendenhall (1906). The Illinois Central took control in 1925 (some sources 1924) and absorbed the company in 1946. Drawn: G&SI main line in two features by opening date (1897-1925, 1900-1925); the Illinois Central era of the whole main line Jackson - Gulfport 1925-1950 as its own feature on identical geometry (Rule 4 split at 1925); the three branch pieces 1901/1906-1918 [OPEN].
sources: Official Guide of the Railways, Feb 1952 issue, IC Tables 25 and 66 (research/sources/official_guide_1952.txt)
not_yet_sourced: [OPEN] Laurel Branch (gsi-laurel-branch): passenger end unknown. Last confirmed year 1918 (Fowler 1918t); freight-only by c. Sept 1951 (Feb 1952 Guide Table 66). Whether any passenger or mixed train ran after the 1925 IC takeover is unknown, so no IC-era branch feature is drawn.

[OPEN] Columbia Branch Maxie - Columbia (gsi-columbia-branch-maxie-columbia): passenger end unknown, last confirmed year 1918 (Fowler 1918t). A forum post (unread, paywalled) says the track was lifted in the mid-1930s. Lumberton - Maxie leased to Edward Hines Yellow Pine Trustees / Mississippi Southern Dec 1924: nature of the lease and whether passengers ran not established.

[OPEN] Columbia Branch Columbia - Mendenhall (gsi-columbia-branch-columbia-mendenhall): passenger end unknown, last confirmed year 1918 (Fowler 1918t). Completion April 1906 (Wikipedia/ICC) vs June 1906 (msrailroads).
Main-line start: 3 Oct 1896 (Wikipedia) vs 1 Jan 1897 (ICC, msrailroads); drawn from 1897.
G&SI -> IC: the exact date the IC began operating the trains (1924, 1925 or only 1946 integration) is not established; split drawn at 1925.
The 17 Nov 1950 last-train day rests on one photo caption seen via a search summary; Nov 1950 is corroborated by Wikipedia and court records.
Any Columbia, Lumberton & Gulf passenger service before 1900 (Fowler 'Florine 1898G') - not dated or drawn.
All headway_min and avg_speed_kmh values are estimates; only the 1950 one-train-each-way figure on the IC main line is sourced (court record).
omitted: Illinois Central Laurel Branch and Columbia Branch after 1925 (report blocks [8], [9]): drawable NONE - no confirmable IC-era passenger year.
Gulfport - Panama Limited through sleeper (block [4]): not a separate line; noted in ic-jackson-gulfport.
Gulfport - Saucier pre-1897 construction stub (block [10]): no passenger evidence before 1897.
Columbia, Lumberton & Gulf predecessor (block [11]) and Laurel & Northwestern / Eastman, Gardiner logging road (block [12]): no datable passenger service.
Laurel - Kingston extension (block [13]) and Gulfport terminal/harbor trackage (block [14]): not passenger lines.
Ripley Railroad / Ship Island, Ripley & Kentucky (block [15]): a different company (Gulf & Chicago / GM&N lineage), not G&SI.
metadata.freight_only_excluded: Jackson - Gulfport after Nov 1950; Laurel Branch freight to c. 1990/1992; Columbia - Silver Creek under IC, Columbia & Silver Creek (1982) and Gloster Southern (1988-1995); MidSouth (1986), KCS (1993) and the 2020 Rock Island Rail 'Gulf and Ship Island' revival - all freight, none drawn (Rule 1).

segments.note: G&SI passenger service Gulfport - Lyman - Saucier - Perkinston - Wiggins - Maxie - Brooklyn - McLaurin - Hattiesburg. START: sources differ - Wikipedia has the line completed Gulfport-Hattiesburg 3 Oct 1896; the ICC valuation and msrailroads say completed to Hattiesburg 1 Jan 1897; HawkinsRails 'did not reach Hattiesburg until 1897'. Drawn from 1897, the later end of the bracket and the first Official Guide appearance of its stations (Fowler: Saucier, Ralston/Enon, Epps/Finley, Griffin all '1897G'). The first ~20 mi Gulfport - Saucier were graded c. 1887-1890, but no passenger operation is documented before the line reached Hattiesburg, so nothing is drawn earlier. END: 1925 is the change of operator to the Illinois Central, not an end of service - trains continued under the IC (see feature ic-jackson-gulfport). The 1925 G&SI -> Illinois Central split rests on IC purchase/control in 1925 (Wikipedia, HawkinsRails, msrailroads; Wikipedia/SNAC say IC subsidiary 'beginning in 1924'); no source found states the date the IC began running the trains, and formal absorption was 1946. By the 1930s-40s the IC certainly ran them (IC Nos. 155/104 in 1942; IC 1950 discontinuance). Through Gulfport - Memphis - Chicago sleepers began Dec 1924 (Wikipedia). headway_min 720 is an estimate (about one train each way a day), not read from a timetable.
sources: Segment-level: dates from Wikipedia (G&SI article), the ICC valuation (vol. 106) summary, msrailroads.com and HawkinsRails as compared in research/branches/gulf_and_ship_island_railroad.txt block [1]; first Guide evidence from Fowler route 33. headway_min not sourced (estimate).

segments.note: Illinois Central operation of the ex-Gulf and Ship Island main line Jackson - Mendenhall - Magee - Saratoga - Collins - Hattiesburg - Wiggins - Saucier - Gulfport (G&SI an IC-controlled subsidiary 1925-1946, absorbed 1946). START: 1925, the year IC control began (Wikipedia, HawkinsRails, msrailroads; some sources say 1924); month not established. The 1925 G&SI -> Illinois Central split rests on IC purchase/control in 1925 (Wikipedia, HawkinsRails, msrailroads; Wikipedia/SNAC say IC subsidiary 'beginning in 1924'); no source found states the date the IC began running the trains, and formal absorption was 1946. By the 1930s-40s the IC certainly ran them (IC Nos. 155/104 in 1942; IC 1950 discontinuance). In 1942 IC trains 155 (dep. Jackson 5:25 am for Gulfport) and 104 (arr. Jackson 1:10 pm from Gulfport) (chicagorailfan.com). A through Gulfport - Chicago sleeper ran Dec 1924 - Nov 1950, handled by the Panama Limited north of Jackson (drawn in illinois_central.geojson; not a separate feature here). END: passenger service ended Nov 1950 (Wikipedia; the 17 Nov 1950 day rests on one photo-archive caption seen only via a search summary). Court records (220 Miss. 439, 1954; 135 F.Supp. 304, 1955): before 1 Oct 1950 the IC ran two daily passenger trains, one each way, Jackson - Gulfport; the PSC ordered service continued 18 Oct 1950 but a temporary injunction restrained enforcement. The Feb 1952 Official Guide prints IC Table 25 Jackson and Gulfport under 'FREIGHT SERVICE ONLY'. Freight continued (Hattiesburg - Gulfport to MidSouth 1986, KCS 1993) and is not drawn (Rule 1). headway_min 720 = one train each way a day per the court record (1950) and the 1942 listing; earlier IC-era frequency not checked.
sources: Segment-level: end from Wikipedia (G&SI article), the court records at leagle.com and the Feb 1952 Official Guide Table 25 (research/sources/official_guide_1952.txt lines 130046-130116, legend 252424); 17 Nov 1950 day from the cahancock rrpicturearchives caption (search summary only); 1942 trains from chicagorailfan.com; start = 1925 IC control per Wikipedia / HawkinsRails / msrailroads, exact operating-change date not established.

segments.note: G&SI Laurel Branch passenger service Saratoga - Mize - Taylorsville - Summerland - Soso - Laurel. START: the branch was completed to Saratoga 31 Aug 1900 (Wikipedia; ICC: turned over to the carrier July 1900), built partly on the 1889 Eastman, Gardiner & Co. (Laurel & Northwestern) logging road, which is not drawn (no passenger evidence; Rule 1). Drawn from 1901, the first positive passenger evidence (Fowler: Mize/Cohay 1901G, Okoha, Betah [Taylorsville], Woodbury [Gitano] in the 1901 Guide list). [OPEN] The 1918 end is the last CONFIRMED year (Fowler's 1918t company public timetable), NOT a known end - no source found dates when branch passenger service actually stopped, and it very likely continued past 1918 by an unknown amount. Do not extend without evidence. The branch was freight-only by c. Sept 1951 (Feb 1952 Guide IC Table 66 'LAUREL BRANCH' in the freight-only block; Index daggers on Laurel and Mize); whether any passenger train survived the 1925 IC takeover is unknown, so no IC-era feature is drawn. Freight continued to c. 1990 beyond Taylorsville and 1992 Taylorsville - Soso. headway_min 1440 is an estimate (a daily branch local, possibly a mixed train), not sourced.
sources: Segment-level: start from Wikipedia / ICC valuation summary and Fowler route 35 (1901G list); end = last confirmed year from Fowler route 35 1918t (Milton, Low, Gambrell); freight-only by 1951 from the Feb 1952 Official Guide Table 66 (research/sources/official_guide_1952.txt ~130680-130702). headway_min not sourced.

Any earlier Columbia, Lumberton & Gulf passenger service (Fowler 'Florine 1898G') belongs to a different company and is not dated or drawn.
